Solec nad Wisla Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Solec nad Wisłą, Poland

Not demolished. Jewish settlement in Solec nad Wisłą dates to the 17th century but expanded mainly in the 19th; by 1921, 735 Jews made up over 43% of the town's population, and most were murdered at Treblinka in late 1942. The cemetery was established around 1889, alongside the founding of the town's synagogue supervision, and remained in active use until the war - its last recorded burials were of Jankiel Dawidson, shot by German gendarmes in April 1942, and four unidentified victims shot in October 1943. Poland closed the cemetery by ministerial order in 1964, by which point it had fallen into ruin; only a handful of sandstone stelae survive today, alongside faint traces of its earthen embankment and stone wall. One recovered tombstone fragment - belonging to a man who died in 1906 - now stands outside the local parish church, next to a monument to John Paul II.
